binders: fmt, universally quantified over floating formats consisting of beta,p,emin,emax with beta,p natural and emin,emax integer.
x1, x2, and x3, universally quantified scalar real numbers.
tr=(th,tl,s1,a2,a3,a4,s2,t,r,s3), a universally quantified ten-component real trace.
run, universally quantified evidence that fmt, the inputs, and tr satisfy the complete execution specification.
hypotheses: The format satisfies 2 <= beta, 0 < p, and emin <= emax.
There are normalized format representations x1Rep, x2Rep, and x3Rep of x1, x2, and x3. If their exponents are e1,e2,e3, each exponent is minimal among all representations of its value.

A valid product split at grids e2 and e3 produces th and tl from x2 and x3. Thus th+tl=x2*x3; th is a nearest representable value to x2*x3; th and tl have normalized representations; the exact product does not overflow; nonzero x2*x3 implies nonzero th; and tl satisfies both split low-part bounds.

A valid product split of x1 and th at grids e1 and e2+e3 produces s1 and a2, and a valid product split of x1 and tl at the same grids produces a3 and a4. Consequently s1+a2=x1*th and a3+a4=x1*tl, with the corresponding representability, nearest-rounding, nonzero-high, no-overflow, and low-part bounds.
s2 is a nearest representable value to a2+a3; t is a nearest representable value to s2-a2; and r is a nearest representable value to a3-t.
The exact values a2+a3, s2-a2, a3-t, and r+a4 satisfy |z| <= maxValue, and s3 is a nearest representable value to r+a4.
conclusions: There exists a representation ra2 of a2 with integer exponent e such that |a3| <= cast(beta^p - beta/2) * (cast beta)^e, where beta^p - beta/2 is computed in Nat and beta/2 is natural floor division.
mathematical_definitions: Let beta_R=cast(beta), scale(e)=beta_R^e for integer e, B=beta_R^p, M=cast(beta^p-1), and maxValue=M*scale(emax).
A representation of x is a pair of integers (m,e) satisfying -B < cast(m) < B, emin <= e <= emax, and x=cast(m)*scale(e).
A normalized representation is a representation whose exponent is less than or equal to the exponent of every representation of the same real.
A nearest rounding of exact to rounded means rounded is representable and |exact-rounded| <= |exact-candidate| for every representable candidate; ties are permitted.

A product split of left and right into high and low includes high+low=left*right, nearest rounding of left*right to high, normalized representations of high and low, nonzero product implying nonzero high, no overflow of the exact product, |low| <= (B/2)*scale(leftGrid+rightGrid), and |low| <= (1/2)*scale(exponent(highRep)).
The merge trace performs nearest rounding of a2+a3 to s2, then s2-a2 to t, then a3-t to r; the run subsequently rounds r+a4 to s3.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every valid radix-beta format, every three real inputs, every ten-real trace, and every execution witness showing that the trace is produced by the specified normalized product splits and nearest-rounding merge under the stated no-overflow conditions, a2 has a format representation whose exponent controls a3 by |a3| <= cast(beta^p-beta/2)*beta_R^exponent. Moreover, the rounded merge operations are exact in the asserted compensated sense: t=s2-a2, r=a3-t, s2+r=a2+a3, and s3=r+a4. The resulting expansion is exact, with (s1+s2)+s3=(x1*x2)*x3.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Although x1, x2, and x3 are quantified over all reals, a run can exist only when all three have normalized representations and all required intermediate product outputs are representable.
For any fmt, inputs, and trace for which the execution type is empty, the theorem imposes no conclusion; the universal binder over run evidence is vacuous there.

The format is finite and bounded: mantissas satisfy strict bounds -beta_R^p < m < beta_R^p and exponents lie between emin and emax. No infinities, NaNs, signed zeros, or other exceptional values are modeled.
Nearest rounding has no tie-breaking rule. Any representable minimizer is allowed.
The coefficient cast(beta^p-beta/2) is computed using natural power, natural floor division, and natural truncated subtraction before conversion to Real.
The first conclusion existentially chooses an ordinary representation of a2; it does not explicitly require that chosen representation to be normalized or unique.
No sign or nonzero assumptions are placed on the inputs. The only nonzero condition is internal to each product split: a nonzero exact product must have a nonzero high part.
noOverflow is only the magnitude condition |z| <= maxValue. It does not itself assert representability, normality, absence of underflow, or exact rounding.
The theorem concerns scalar real arithmetic only; it encodes no vector, matrix, normed-space, or dimensional statement.

The final equality is an exact expansion identity. It does not claim that s1+s2+s3 is itself representable, rounded once, or free of overflow when evaluated as a subsequent floating-point computation.
ambiguities: The internal constructors of Nat.AtLeastTwo are not supplied, so that predicate cannot be independently unfolded from the packet. Its uses only justify numeral instances, and D102 explicitly fixes each resulting numeral to the corresponding natural cast, leaving the mathematical target unambiguous.
